etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Ultimate derivation currently unknown, with various resources listing no etymology. Theories include:
* Perhaps related to interjection は (ha, “yes”), which first appears in the early 1600s.
* Alternatively, may perhaps from Sino-Japanese 拝 (hai), but this theory is not academically accepted.
First cited as a general shout in the early 1600s (compare English hey), with the affirmative yes sense first cited to 1774.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 初(そ)める (someru, “(of an action) to begin, to be begun; (of such an action or its result) to continue for a long time”, auxiliary verb attaching to another verb's 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei)), in turn likely cognate with 染(そ)める (someru, “to dye something”, when used as an auxiliary, “to do something deeply or thoroughly”).
The verb is first attested in this kind of auxiliary sense in the Man'yōshū of 759.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from 初(そ)め (some) above. The so changes to zo as an instance of rendaku (連濁).
